#### 1. NF2-related schwannomatosis  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.778)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-2029482, Reactome:R-HSA-5627123)

**Proposed mechanism:** NF2 (HGNC:7773) —DISRUPTS→ Merlin (NF2 protein) (HGNC:7773); Merlin (NF2 protein) (HGNC:7773) —DISRUPTS→ Cell-cell junction regulation (GO:0034330); Cell-cell junction regulation (GO:0034330) —LEADS_TO→ Meningioma (HP:0002370); Cell-cell junction regulation (GO:0034330) —LEADS_TO→ Schwannoma (HP:0000978). Loss-of-function mutations in the NF2 gene lead to a dysfunctional Merlin protein, which disrupts the regulation of cell-cell junctions. This disruption in turn promotes the development of both meningiomas (familial meningioma) and schwannomas (NF2-related schwannomatosis).

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in NF2 that are exclusively associated with one disease and not the other, or the discovery of distinct, non-overlapping molecular pathways for each disease in individuals with different NF2 mutations. _(variant: rs121918472)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism involving NF2 and cell-cell junction regulation could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting these pathways for both familial meningioma and NF2-related schwannomatosis, potentially improving treatment outcomes for patients with either condition.
